topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning outcomes regarding carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Biological basis and origins of oncogenic mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the fundamental biology of cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease driven by endogenous, environmental, and inherited sources of mutation.

topics.label: Environmental exposures and epidemiological patterns of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for environmental cancer causes by examining lifestyle exposures, the role of chance, and geographical variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral mechanisms in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how infectious pathogens contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma as a primary mechanistic model.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and metabolically activated chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and two-stage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the concept of tumor promotion, illustrating how non-mutagenic factors drive cancer development through chronic inflammation and proliferative signaling.

topics.label: Developmental susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how host developmental timing influences cancer susceptibility and provide a consolidated summary of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and determine carcinogenic risk.
